clue.text: Environment inside marsh a bit atypical

indicators.note: something inside is contained within the surrounding words, so the answer sits concealed in the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of the first word through the middle to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Something about the surroundings in a wetland seems a little unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles four words: the tail of 'marsh', then 'a', 'bit', and the opening of 'atypical'.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or surroundings of a plant or animal, so it is a synonym for environment.

clue.text: Shade house regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a house regularly in the shade, or to paint it a colour routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' looks like a verb about keeping a house cool; it is the noun for a tint of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a particular colour or tint, which is exactly what a shade of paint or light is.

clue.text: Forbid one to leave peaceful feast

parts.note: to ban something is to forbid it

indicators.note: whatever leaves a word departs from it, so that letter is removed from the word beside it

parts.note: a synonym; with the numeral gone it becomes QUET
the Roman numeral for one, the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone wants to stop a person from walking out of a calm, pleasant dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: BAN plus QUIET with its I dropped gives BAN + QUET. The single letter I standing for one is a Roman numeral convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is an elaborate formal meal for many guests, so it is a grand version of a feast.

clue.text: Coach's expression of annoyance, alternatively

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound people make when irritated
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A sports coach mutters something irritated, or perhaps something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor gives private instruction to a student, which is what a coach does in academic subjects.

clue.text: He'd turn off loud noise?

indicators.note: food that is off has gone bad, so these letters have spoiled into a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man would switch off some racket if he could.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn off' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'turn' is fodder and 'off' alone is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is the booming sound that follows lightning, the classic example of a very loud noise.

clue.text: Piece of music expected before end of concert

parts.note: something due is expected to arrive

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A particular item on the programme is scheduled to be played just before a concert finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' places DUE ahead of the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is a musical composition for two performers, so it is one kind of piece of music.

clue.text: Detective with journal primarily on French city

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police investigator keeps a diary mostly about a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: DI, a Detective Inspector, is a standard crossword abbreviation from British policing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dijon is a city in eastern France, capital of Burgundy and famous for its mustard.

clue.text: Greet sage cooking seasonal treat

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients by mixing them up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Welcome the herb that is being used to make a holiday dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb going into the pot, but it and 'Greet' supply the letters, and 'cooking' is what scrambles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs are given and eaten around the spring Christian holiday, making them a treat tied to one time of year.

clue.text: Somewhat overhype a nutritious edible seed

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following letters is used

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across the middle into the third

explanation.surface: Someone is exaggerating how healthy a certain kernel is.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the tail of 'overhype', takes 'a', and ends partway into 'nutritious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a peanut is the seed of a legume plant, and people eat it roasted or as butter.

clue.text: International organisation simply not fair

parts.note: the United Nations
just as in 'it's just a game', meaning simply

explanation.surface: A complaint that a global body is behaving plainly inequitably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International organisation' looks like the subject of a sentence; it is just the two-letter UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unjust violates justice or equity, which is what treating people unfairly amounts to.

clue.text: Nerdy European hosting start of costly activity for couples

parts.note: a square is an unfashionable, conventional person

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a Dane is a person from Denmark

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A geeky person from Europe organises the beginning of an expensive date-night pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nerdy' reads as a description of the European, but it is a separate piece: square is old slang for someone dull and conventional.
explanation.definitionFit: In a square dance four pairs of partners face each other in a square, so it is a pastime done in couples.

clue.text: Phew — Rick's sorted out disaster at sea

indicators.note: to sort something out is to rearrange it into order, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Relief: a man named Rick has resolved a maritime catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' reads as Rick fixing the problem, but it signals rearranging the letters of 'Phew' and 'Rick's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwreck is the destruction or sinking of a vessel, the archetypal catastrophe on the ocean.

clue.text: Winner is Frankenstein, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who triumphs in a contest
second meaning: the first name of the scientist in Mary Shelley's novel

explanation.walkthrough: Frankenstein is the scientist, not the monster, and his first name is the word for a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for someone who defeats an opponent, and also the given name of Shelley's scientist, Frankenstein.

clue.text: Withdraw extremely rude nurse

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outermost letters of the word
to nurse a patient is to treat them

explanation.surface: Pull back from a very impolite hospital worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' looks like a noun for the rude person, but it is the verb meaning to care for medically.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to move back or pull away, a synonym for withdraw, especially of troops.

clue.text: It supports whitewater enthusiast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sloping beam holding up a roof
second meaning: someone who goes rafting down rapids

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a thing that backs a fan of rapids; the first meaning is a roof timber, the second a person who rafts.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a structural roof beam, and by adding -er to raft it also names a person riding rapids on an inflatable.

clue.text: Right to split healthier bit of fried food

indicators.note: splitting something opens it up, so one piece goes into the gap made in the other

parts.note: fitter means in better health
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone argues they are entitled to divide a healthier portion of deep-fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes between the F and I of FITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fritter is a small piece of fruit, vegetable or meat coated in batter and deep-fried.

clue.text: Drinks event to secure arrival time — smart!

parts.note: to win something is to secure it
estimated time of arrival
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Clever idea: guarantee when guests turn up to a drinks party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like praise for being clever, but it is the verb meaning to hurt sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine tasting is a gathering where people sample several wines, so it is a social occasion centred on drinks.

clue.text: What a baby needs — sleep and empty potty?

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A list of an infant's needs: a snooze and a potty that has been emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: A nappy is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A nappy is the absorbent pad or garment worn by an infant who is not yet toilet trained, an essential item for them.

clue.text: Capture bodies of water, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: seas are large bodies of salt water

explanation.surface: News that someone has taken control of some lakes or oceans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capture' seems to act on the waters, but it is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize is to take hold of forcibly, which is what capturing a person or place involves.

clue.text: Place for worshipping part of head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a building used for religious worship
second meaning: the flat area at each side of the forehead

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the head of a church; the two halves are separate meanings, a religious building and a spot beside the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a sacred building for religious services and the flat side region of the skull between eye and ear.

clue.text: Bury institution's last trainee

parts.note: to inter is to put a body in a grave

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A town called Bury has an institution with a final apprentice on its books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' is capitalised to look like the English town near Manchester; it is the verb meaning to put in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a junior worker or student gaining practical experience, which makes them a trainee.

clue.text: Liquor and cut of beef unfinished

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rump is a cut from the hindquarters; losing its last letter leaves the first three

explanation.surface: A half-eaten steak with a glass of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMP loses its final P.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane, one of the classic kinds of hard liquor.

clue.text: Fine with duck and bovine returning

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox

explanation.surface: A water bird and a cow come back, and all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out for zero scores a duck, so duck gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is an informal way of saying something is acceptable or satisfactory, which fine also expresses.

clue.text: Met hero developing proposition

indicators.note: developing means changing into something new, so these letters change their order

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Someone encountered a champion who was working up a business offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proposition' suggests a business proposal, but here it means a statement to be proved, as in mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a statement proved from axioms, and proposition is the formal name for such a statement.
